title: Loops that run zero times
idea: A while loop checks its condition first, so it may not run at all.

exercises.prompt: A while loop checks its condition BEFORE the first pass. What if the condition is false right away?
options: The loop body runs zero times
exercises.explanation: while tests first. If the condition starts false, the body is skipped entirely -- zero passes.

exercises.prompt:
What shows?

i = 5
while i < 3:
    print(i)
print("done")
exercises.explanation: 5 < 3 is false from the start, so the loop body never runs. Only the line after the loop, 'done', prints.

exercises.prompt: A while loop always runs at least once.
exercises.explanation: False. Because it checks first, a while loop can run zero times if the condition starts false.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'runs zero times' sometimes exactly what you want?
options: If there's nothing to do, the loop should do nothing
exercises.explanation: A loop over 'remaining items' should do nothing when there are none. Checking first makes that natural and safe.

exercises.prompt:
What shows?

n = 0
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n = n - 1
print("empty")
exercises.explanation: n > 0 is false at the start (0 > 0 is false), so the body is skipped. Only 'empty' prints.

exercises.prompt: Which while loops run their body ZERO times?
exercises.explanation: First two have conditions false at the start, so zero passes. The last two are true at the start and do run.

exercises.prompt: Order these outcomes from fewest to most passes for i starting at 2.
blocks: while i < 3: (1 pass, then update to 3)
exercises.explanation: i = 2: i > 5 is false (0 passes); i < 3 runs once; i < 5 runs for 2,3,4 (3 passes). Checking first explains all three.

exercises.prompt:
Make this loop run ZERO times by choosing a start value. Fill the start so the body is skipped:

i = ____
while i < 3:
    print(i)
exercises.explanation: Any start that already fails i < 3 works -- e.g. i = 3 makes 3 < 3 false, so the body never runs.

exercises.prompt: Because while checks first, you can safely write a loop even when it might have nothing to do.
exercises.explanation: True. The check-first behavior means an empty case simply skips the body -- no special handling needed.

exercises.prompt: 'Check the condition first' means a while loop is good for...
options: Work that might not need to happen at all
Work that must happen exactly once
exercises.explanation: When the job might be empty, checking first lets the loop do nothing gracefully. That's a feature, not a bug.
